warning.policy-any-any_other: {{count}} policies allow everything: source all, destination all, service ALL.

problems.unverifiedNote: One of the values is the default of this version, not confirmed yet on real devices: check it on the device.

problems.deviceIntro_other: The consistency checks between the devices of the client found {{count}} problems about this device.

ipsec-no-tunnel.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}}: no tunnel on {{b}} accepts the peer
ipsec-no-tunnel.why: The tunnel {{tunnelA}} of {{a}} points to {{peer}}, the interface {{interface}} of {{b}}, but no phase 1 on that interface of {{b}} accepts {{a}}: the tunnel does not come up.
ipsec-no-tunnel.fix: On {{b}} create the tunnel to {{a}} on {{interface}}, or correct the remote gateway of {{tunnelA}} on {{a}}.

ipsec-ike.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: different IKE version
ipsec-ike.why: {{a}} uses {{valueA}}, {{b}} uses {{valueB}}: with different versions phase 1 cannot be negotiated.
ipsec-ike.fix: Set the same IKE version (ike-version) on both sides.

ipsec-mode.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: different IKEv1 mode
ipsec-mode.why: {{a}} is in {{valueA}} mode, {{b}} in {{valueB}}: with IKEv1 both sides must use the same mode.
ipsec-mode.fix: Set the same mode (main or aggressive) on both sides.

ipsec-auth.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: different authentication
ipsec-auth.why: {{a}} authenticates with {{valueA}}, {{b}} with {{valueB}}: phase 1 does not complete.
ipsec-auth.fix: Use the same method (authmethod) on both sides: pre-shared key or certificates.

ipsec-proposals.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: no phase 1 proposal in common
ipsec-proposals.why: {{a}} proposes {{valueA}}, {{b}} proposes {{valueB}}: without at least one encryption and integrity pair in common phase 1 cannot be negotiated.
ipsec-proposals.fix: Add on one side one of the proposals of the other (set proposal), the strongest one if possible.

ipsec-dhgrp.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: no phase 1 DH group in common
ipsec-dhgrp.why: {{a}} uses the groups {{valueA}}, {{b}} the groups {{valueB}}: without a Diffie-Hellman group in common phase 1 cannot be negotiated.
ipsec-dhgrp.fix: Put at least one DH group in common on both sides (set dhgrp), for example 14, 19 or 20.

ipsec-selectors.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: phase 2 selectors do not mirror each other
ipsec-selectors.why: The phases 2 of {{a}} ({{valueA}}) find on {{b}} ({{valueB}}) no phase 2 with source and destination swapped: that traffic does not go into the tunnel.
ipsec-selectors.fix: The source of a phase 2 must be the destination on the other side: correct src-subnet and dst-subnet.

ipsec-p2-proposals.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: no phase 2 proposal in common
ipsec-p2-proposals.why: A phase 2 of {{a}} proposes {{valueA}}, the mirror one of {{b}} proposes {{valueB}}: phase 2 cannot be negotiated.
ipsec-p2-proposals.fix: Put at least one phase 2 proposal in common on both sides.

ipsec-pfs.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: PFS on one side only
ipsec-pfs.why: PFS is on one side only ({{a}}: {{valueA}}, {{b}}: {{valueB}}): phase 2 cannot be negotiated.
ipsec-pfs.fix: Turn PFS (set pfs) on or off on both sides, with the same DH groups.

ipsec-p2-dhgrp.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: no phase 2 DH group in common
ipsec-p2-dhgrp.why: With PFS on, {{a}} uses the groups {{valueA}} and {{b}} the groups {{valueB}}: phase 2 cannot be negotiated.
ipsec-p2-dhgrp.fix: Put at least one phase 2 DH group in common on both sides.

ipsec-advpn.title: {{a}} {{tunnelA}} ↔ {{b}} {{tunnelB}}: wrong ADVPN roles
ipsec-advpn.why: {{a}} is {{valueA}}, {{b}} is {{valueB}}: shortcuts start only with the dial-up hub as sender and the branch as receiver.
ipsec-advpn.fix: Set auto-discovery-sender on the hub and auto-discovery-receiver on the branch.

bgp-down.title: BGP session {{a}} ↔ {{b}} not established
bgp-down.why: In the shows the session to {{ip}} is in the state "{{state}}": no routes pass between the two devices.
bgp-down.viaDown: The session goes through the tunnel {{via}}, which is down in the shows: look at the tunnel first.
bgp-down.viaProblem: The session goes through the tunnel {{via}}, which has configuration problems: look at them first.
bgp-down.viaUp: The session goes through the tunnel {{via}}, which is up in the shows: check the neighbors, the AS numbers and the policies of the session.
bgp-down.fix: Check that neighbors and AS numbers match on both sides and that BGP traffic (TCP 179) passes between {{a}} and {{b}}.

bgp-no-neighbor.title: {{b}} has no BGP neighbor {{ip}} of {{a}}
bgp-no-neighbor.why: {{a}} opens a BGP session to {{b}} from the address {{ip}}, but {{b}} has no neighbor nor neighbor-range that covers it: the session does not come up.
bgp-no-neighbor.fix: On {{b}} add the neighbor {{ip}} with the AS of {{a}}, or a neighbor-range that covers it.

bgp-as.title: {{device}} expects AS {{expected}} from {{peer}}, which has AS {{actual}}
bgp-as.why: The remote-as of the neighbor is not the AS of {{peer}}: the session closes as soon as it opens.
bgp-as.fix: Correct the remote-as on {{device}}, or the AS of {{peer}}.

trunk-mode.title: {{a}} {{portA}} ↔ {{b}} {{portB}}: trunk modes do not match
trunk-mode.why: {{portA}} is {{valueA}}, {{portB}} is {{valueB}}: one side sends the VLANs tagged and the other does not, or both wait for the other to propose the trunk. The VLANs do not pass.
trunk-mode.fix: Put both sides in trunk mode (switchport mode trunk), or both in access mode on the same VLAN.

trunk-native.title: {{a}} {{portA}} ↔ {{b}} {{portB}}: different native VLAN
trunk-native.why: The native VLAN is {{valueA}} on {{a}} and {{valueB}} on {{b}}: untagged traffic ends up in different VLANs on the two sides.
trunk-native.fix: Set the same native VLAN (switchport trunk native vlan) on both sides.

trunk-allowed.title: {{a}} {{portA}} ↔ {{b}} {{portB}}: different allowed VLANs
trunk-allowed.why: Only on {{a}}: {{onlyA}}. Only on {{b}}: {{onlyB}}. VLANs allowed on one side only do not pass on the link.
trunk-allowed.fix: Align the allowed VLANs (switchport trunk allowed vlan) on both sides, or remove the ones that are not needed.

lag-one-side.title: {{a}} {{portA}} ↔ {{b}} {{portB}}: aggregate on one side only
lag-one-side.why: On {{lag}} the ports are in an aggregate, on {{single}} they are not: the cables work as separate links and can create loops or lose traffic.
lag-one-side.fix: Configure the aggregate on {{single}} too, with the same ports and the same protocol.

lag-mode.title: {{a}} {{portA}} ↔ {{b}} {{portB}}: LAG protocols do not match
lag-mode.why: {{a}} uses {{valueA}}, {{b}} uses {{valueB}}: with these modes the port-channel does not form and the ports stay suspended.
lag-mode.fix: Use the same protocol on both sides: LACP (active on at least one side) or static (on) on both.

lag-cables.title: {{a}} {{portA}} ↔ {{b}} {{portB}}: different number of ports in the LAG
lag-cables.why: The aggregate has {{valueA}} ports on {{a}} and {{valueB}} on {{b}}: a cable is not in the aggregate on one of the two sides.
lag-cables.fix: Put the same ports in the aggregate on both sides, or check the cables.

mtu.title: {{a}} {{portA}} ↔ {{b}} {{portB}}: different MTU
mtu.why: The MTU is {{valueA}} on {{a}} and {{valueB}} on {{b}}: packets bigger than the smaller side are dropped or fragmented.
mtu.fix: Set the same MTU on both sides.

ospf-area.title: {{a}} {{portA}} ↔ {{b}} {{portB}}: different OSPF area
ospf-area.why: {{portA}} is in area {{valueA}}, {{portB}} in area {{valueB}}: the OSPF adjacency does not form.
ospf-area.fix: Put the two interfaces in the same area.

ospf-passive.title: {{a}} {{portA}} ↔ {{b}} {{portB}}: OSPF interface passive on one side
ospf-passive.why: On {{passive}} the interface is passive: it sends no hello and the adjacency on this network does not form.
ospf-passive.fix: If the adjacency is needed, remove the passive interface (no passive-interface); if not, make the other interface passive too.

ip-duplicate.title: Duplicate address {{ip}}
ip-duplicate.why: The same address is on {{where}}: traffic to {{ip}} reaches only one of them, and the routes to that network become ambiguous.
ip-duplicate.fix: Change the address on one of the two devices; if the interface is not used, remove its address.

subnet-overlap.title: Subnet {{subnet}} in more than one site
subnet-overlap.why: The same network is in different sites: {{where}}. If the sites talk through VPN or routing, traffic to that network takes one way only.
subnet-overlap.fix: Renumber one of the networks, or keep it local without announcing it to the other sites.

route-missing.title: {{device}} has no route to {{prefix}}
route-missing.why: {{from}} announces {{prefix}} in BGP, but the routing table of {{device}} (in the shows) does not have that network: traffic to {{prefix}} does not arrive.
route-missing.fix: Check the BGP session, the filters (route-map, prefix-list) and that the hub reflects the network to the branches.

description-mismatch.title: {{device}} {{port}}: the description says {{described}}, {{protocol}} sees {{seen}}
description-mismatch.why: The description of the port ("{{description}}") names {{described}}, but {{protocol}} sees {{seen}} on this port: the description is old or the cable is in the wrong port.
description-mismatch.fix: Correct the description, or move the cable to the right port.

discovery-off.title: {{device}} {{port}}: LLDP and CDP off
discovery-off.why: The cable comes from the description of the port, but on {{device}} LLDP and CDP are off on this port: a show cannot confirm it.
discovery-off.fix: If the client's rules allow it, turn LLDP or CDP on and load the show of the neighbors.

advpn-hub-policy.title: {{hub}}: no policy between the overlays
advpn-hub-policy.why: Two branches talk through the hub until the shortcut is up, but on {{hub}} ({{vdom}}) no policy, and no zone with intra-zone traffic allowed, lets traffic pass from an overlay to another.
advpn-hub-policy.fix: On {{hub}} add a policy from the overlays to the overlays, or allow the traffic inside the zone (intrazone allow).

advpn-spoke-policy.title: {{device}}: no policy to the other branches
advpn-spoke-policy.why: The policies of {{device}} to the tunnels of {{hub}} do not cover the networks of the other branches: the first traffic to them is blocked and the shortcut does not start.
advpn-spoke-policy.fix: Add the networks of the other branches to the policy to the overlay, for example with an address group.

advpn-next-hop.title: {{hub}}: BGP changes the next hop to the branches
advpn-next-hop.why: The BGP group {{group}} of {{hub}} has next-hop-self: the branches get the networks of the others with the hub as next hop and traffic does not use the shortcut.
advpn-next-hop.fix: Remove next-hop-self from the group of the branches on the hub.

advpn-no-rr.title: {{hub}}: the networks of the branches are not reflected
advpn-no-rr.why: The branches are iBGP neighbors of {{hub}}, but none of their groups is a route reflector client: a branch does not learn the networks of the others.
advpn-no-rr.fix: On the hub set route-reflector-client in the groups of the branches.

vpnClient.title: VPN of the client
vpnClient.summary: {{tunnels}} between the devices, {{shortcuts}} in the shows
vpnClient.none: No IPsec tunnel between the loaded devices.
vpnClient.hint: Click a tunnel to see its two sides next to each other, parameter by parameter, with the problems and the lines they come from.

compare.noTunnel: no tunnel on the other side

advpn.title: ADVPN
advpn.intro: The hub (sender) tells the branches (receivers) how to reach each other: traffic between two branches starts through the hub and then moves to a direct shortcut between them.
advpn.checksOk: No problems: roles, policies and the BGP of the hub allow the shortcuts.
advpn.noPairs: No pair of branches on the same hub.

pair.activeWhy: Seen in the shows: the two branches already talk directly.
pair.possibleWhy: Nothing blocks it in the configurations: it starts with the first traffic between the two branches.
pair.down: The tunnels to the hub are down in the shows.
